messages.subject: scantwo - 2 QTL interactions
parts:
I have been using the QTL package in R for my analysis. It worked very well for the scanone and with the addition of covariates. However, I have some queries about running scantwo which I could not really find answers in the forum or on the web.

1. Does scantwo do (all markers) x (all markers) or is it only the scanone identified QTLs? If only scanone identified QTLs, at what cut-off is that considered?

2. Is there anyway I could choose a specific QTL marker and do a QTL interaction analysis across the whole genome for that marker?

Thanking you in advance.

Regards,
Aparna.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scantwo - 2 QTL interactions
parts:
>
> 1. Does scantwo do (all markers) x (all markers) or is it only the scanone identified QTLs? If only scanone identified QTLs, at what cut-off is that considered?
It does all markers x all markers

>
> 2. Is there anyway I could choose a specific QTL marker and do a QTL interaction analysis across the whole genome for that marker?
>

You can use makeqtl() to create a QTL object with the first locus and then addqtl() to do a scan for a 2nd QTL to add.

Here's an example:

data(fake.bc)
fake.bc <- calc.genoprob(fake.bc, step=1)
out <- scanone(fake.bc, method="hk")
max(out)
qtl <- makeqtl(fake.bc, chr=5, pos=17, what="prob")
out.aq <- addqtl(fake.bc, qtl=qtl, method="hk")
out.iq <- addqtl(fake.bc, qtl=qtl, method="hk", formula= y ~ Q1*Q2,
require.fullrank=FALSE)
plot(out.iq, out.aq, out.iq - out.aq)

The require.fullrank=FALSE in the second addqtl() seems to be necessary in this case; I should change it to the default.

karl
